title: Core building blocks: consistent hashing, bloom filters, quorum, gossip, HLL, geohash
relevance: High — these are the “name the primitive” follow-ups in almost every HLD round (distributed cache/DB, crawler, analytics, proximity/Uber-Yelp); campus + experienced; FAANG and Indian product cos.
company_notes: Campus/new-grad HLD: consistent hashing on cache/URL shortener/chat; Bloom on crawler or username-taken checks; geohash on Yelp/Uber-lite; light quorum wording on Cassandra/Dynamo. Experienced (1–4+ YOE): R+W>N tuning, sloppy quorum, gossip failure detection, HLL analytics counters, H3 vs geohash — Meta, Google, Amazon, Uber, Flipkart, Atlassian infra. High as toolkit follow-ups inside larger designs; rare as standalone “design HyperLogLog”; interviewers want correct tool choice and tradeoffs, not paper proofs.

phases.goal: Name each primitive, what question it answers, and the one invariant interviewers expect.

must_hit.point: Consistent hashing places nodes and keys on a ring; a key maps to the first node clockwise; add/remove moves about K/N keys, not almost all as with hash % N.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws or narrates the ring, clockwise owner lookup, and contrasts minimal remapping with mod-N thrash.

must_hit.point: A Bloom filter is probabilistic set membership: answers “definitely not” or “probably yes”; false positives are OK, false negatives never.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the definitely-not / probably-yes contract and that false negatives are forbidden.

must_hit.point: Dynamo-style quorum: with replication factor N, require W write acks and R read responses; R + W > N means the read set overlaps a successful write; typical N=3, R=W=2.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Defines N/R/W, states R+W>N for recency overlap, and cites the typical N=3, R=W=2 setting.

must_hit.point: Gossip is epidemic peer-to-peer dissemination of membership/heartbeats (not agreeing on one value); HyperLogLog approximates cardinality in tiny fixed memory; geohash encodes (lat, lon) to a base32 string where shared prefix means same/nearby cell.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates gossip-as-membership from consensus, HLL-as-count-distinct, and geohash prefix locality.

probes: Name the six primitives and, for each, the one question it answers in an HLD (placement, membership test, replica freshness, cluster membership, count distinct, nearby).

hints.1: Think toolkit labels: ring, set-maybe, R/W, epidemic membership, approx distinct, geo cells.
hints.2: For each: what it guarantees (or deliberately does not)—especially Bloom FN vs FP and gossip vs consensus.
hints.3: Ring + clockwise owner (~K/N moves); Bloom definitely-not/probably-yes (no FN); R+W>N with typical N=3,R=W=2; gossip disseminates membership; HLL≈cardinality; geohash base32 prefix⇒nearby.

phases.goal: Explain how each primitive works enough to defend the usual follow-up knobs (vnodes, Bloom ops, sloppy quorum, gossip cadence, HLL merge, neighbor query).

must_hit.point: Virtual nodes put many ring positions on one physical node to smooth load and spread failover; consistent hashing does not fix celebrity hot keys—those need salt or replication.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions many vnodes per node for balance/failover and separately calls out hot-key salting/replication.

must_hit.point: Bloom filter = bit array + k hashes; cannot delete (unless counting Bloom); interview uses include crawl “seen?” gates, cache negative lookups, and LSM/SSTable “key might be here?” before disk.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes bit vector + k hashes, no ordinary delete, and at least one of crawl/cache-negative/LSM skip-disk uses.

must_hit.point: Sloppy quorum + hinted handoff keeps writes available when home replicas are down (weaker overlap guarantee); quorum also trades latency (wait for the slowest of R/W) against durability/freshness.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains writing to reachable replicas with later hint replay, and that R/W waits cost latency for stronger freshness.

must_hit.point: Gossip converges in O(log n) rounds with no central registry SPOF; Cassandra-style ~1s exchange to a few peers plus Phi accrual suspicion—contrast ZooKeeper/etcd consensus used for coordination, not membership gossip.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States epidemic convergence, ~1s peer gossip + Phi suspicion, and that ZK/etcd is for coordination agreement not membership flood.

must_hit.point: HLL hashes into registers tracking max leading zeros, is mergeable (e.g. PFMERGE), and in Redis is about 12 KB with about 0.81% standard error; geohash nearby queries use the center cell plus 8 neighbors then an exact distance (Haversine) post-filter—H3 hex k-rings are the Uber-style alternative.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions leading-zeros registers, mergeability, ~12 KB/~0.81%, and 8-neighbor (or 3×3) + exact refine / H3 k-ring.

probes: How do virtual nodes change failover on a hash ring, and how does a Dynamo-style store combine preference lists, R/W quorum, and gossip membership?

hints.1: Start from one physical node owning many ring points, then ask what happens when it dies.
hints.2: Add Bloom’s bit-array mechanics, then sloppy quorum when home replicas are down, then gossip vs ZK.
hints.3: Vnodes spread load/failover (not hot keys); Bloom=bits+k hashes, no delete; sloppy+hints for availability; gossip O(log n)/~1s+Phi vs ZK coordination; HLL leading zeros/~12KB/~0.81% mergeable; geo=center+8 neighbors then Haversine, or H3.

phases.goal: Choose the right primitive and tuning (R/W, Bloom size, gossip vs consensus, HLL vs exact, geohash vs H3) for the design constraint.

must_hit.point: hash % N remaps almost all keys when N changes; consistent hashing moves about K/N; drawing a ring without vnodes invites load skew and “dead node dumps all traffic on one neighbor.”
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts mod-N thrash with ~K/N moves and explains why vnodes matter for skew/failover dump.

must_hit.point: Bloom sizing: lower target FPR (e.g. 1% vs 0.01%) needs a larger bit array; undersizing raises false positives; you still never get a false negative; “yes” must hit the source of truth.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Links bit-array size to FPR, forbids FN, and says positives are verified against the real store.

must_hit.point: For N=3, (R=1,W=1) is weak on freshness; (R=2,W=2) is the common balanced choice; (R=3,W=1) or W=N strengthens durability/freshness at higher write latency and write availability cost when nodes are down.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares those N=3 configurations on stale reads, surviving a down node for writes, and when W=N is chosen.

must_hit.point: Pick tools by job: gossip for membership dissemination vs ZooKeeper/etcd for coordination; Bloom ≠ HLL (membership filter vs cardinality); HLL is wrong for exact billing/invoices; square geohash neighbor rings vs H3 hex k-rings for marketplace/dispatch edge cases.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States each pair’s job boundary and refuses HLL for exact invoice distincts / Bloom for counting.

probes: N=3: compare (R=1,W=1), (R=2,W=2), and (R=3,W=1)—which can return stale reads, which survives one node down for writes, and when do you set W=N?

hints.1: Use R+W>N as the freshness rule of thumb, then stress availability when replicas are down.
hints.2: Map each (R,W) to stale-read risk and write availability; separately say Bloom size↔FPR and gossip≠consensus.
hints.3: R+W>N⇒overlap; typical R=W=2; W=N for strongest write durability; undersized Bloom↑FP never FN; gossip membership vs ZK coordination; HLL≠exact billing; H3 when hex k-rings beat square neighbors.

phases.goal: Compose the primitives into Dynamo-family, analytics, and location paths and attack the standard ≤2 min drills.

must_hit.point: Dynamo-family stack = consistent hashing (placement) + quorum (consistency knobs) + gossip (membership); analytics path = Bloom (filter) + HLL (count); location path = geohash/H3 index + post-filter.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names the three composition recipes and assigns each primitive to placement, consistency, membership, filter, count, or geo index.

must_hit.point: Cache cluster 4→5 nodes: explain why hash % N thrashes, walk a key’s ring owner before/after adding a vnode-rich node, and state that roughly K/N keys move.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates mod-N remapping storm, one key’s clockwise owner change, and ~K/N movement with vnodes.

must_hit.point: Product drills: unique-visitors dashboard prefers HLL over a Redis SET (merge hourly HLLs into daily); user on a geohash cell edge can miss a place 50 m away if only one cell is queried—use 9-cell (center+8) + Haversine, or name H3 for hex k-rings.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Rejects SET for huge uniques, mentions mergeable HLLs, and sketches boundary miss → 9-cell/Haversine or H3.

probes: Design a Cassandra-like KV vs a Kafka controller election: where do you use gossip for membership, and where do you need consensus? What goes wrong if gossip is briefly partitioned?
Nearby restaurants: user sits on a geohash edge—why does one-cell query miss a place 50 m away, and how do you fix it?

hints.1: Ask which subsystem needs membership gossip versus a single agreed leader/value.
hints.2: Compose hashing+quorum+gossip for the KV; contrast controller election; for geo expand to neighbors then exact distance.
hints.3: KV: ring placement + R/W + gossip membership; controller election needs consensus; split gossip⇒split UP/DOWN view; geo: 9-cell/3×3 + Haversine (or H3); HLL for DAU-style uniques, mergeable, not invoices.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: mod-N remaps almost all keys when the cluster size changes; a hash ring moves about K/N keys on add/remove—use consistent hashing (or equivalent minimal-remap slot schemes) for caches, partitions, and sticky LBs.

tradeoffs.topic: Virtual nodes vs single position per node
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Vnodes smooth load and spread failover so a dead node does not dump all traffic onto one clockwise neighbor; they still do not fix celebrity hot keys—salt or replicate those.

Higher R/W waits for the slowest replica and improves overlap/freshness when R+W>N (typical N=3, R=W=2); lower R/W cuts latency but risks stale reads; W=N maximizes write durability at availability cost.

tradeoffs.topic: Strict quorum vs sloppy quorum + hinted handoff
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Strict home-replica quorum preserves stronger R/W overlap; sloppy quorum writes to reachable nodes and hints handoff later to keep writes available when home replicas are down, with a weaker overlap guarantee.

Gossip eventually disseminates membership/heartbeats without a registry SPOF; coordination that must agree on one value/leader (e.g. Kafka controller election) needs a consensus store—gossip does not give strong data consistency by itself.

tradeoffs.topic: Bloom filter vs exact set/DB for membership
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Bloom saves memory/IOPS as a “definitely not / probably yes” gate (crawl seen?, cache negatives, LSM skip-disk); positives must check the source of truth; exact sets/DBs when you need certainty or deletes.

tradeoffs.topic: HLL vs Redis SET for cardinality
tradeoffs.strong_answer: HLL gives approximate distinct counts in tiny fixed memory (~12 KB, ~0.81% error) and merges cleanly; a SET stores members exactly but will not scale the same way for huge uniques—never use HLL for exact billing or enumerating IDs.

tradeoffs.topic: Geohash neighbor ring vs H3 hex k-ring
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Geohash: prefix lookup on center cell + 8 neighbors then Haversine refine; H3’s hex k-rings handle marketplace/surge/dispatch neighbor geometry more cleanly than square geohash edges.
Bloom answers set membership (filter); HLL answers how many distinct (cardinality)—pick the probabilistic structure that matches the question; they are not interchangeable.

gotchas.trap: Drawing a hash ring without virtual nodes
gotchas.correction: Interviewer will probe load skew and “all traffic from a dead node dumps onto one neighbor”—add vnodes; still salt/replicate celebrity hot keys.

gotchas.trap: Treating Bloom “yes” as proof of existence
gotchas.correction: Hit the source of truth on positives; Bloom only reliably saves work on definite negatives.

gotchas.trap: Confusing consensus quorum (Raft majority for one log) with Dynamo quorum (R/W overlap for replica freshness)
gotchas.correction: Say which you mean: majority agreement on one value/order versus R/W overlap for recency across replicas.
Gossip eventually spreads membership; data consistency still needs R/W quorums or a consensus store.

gotchas.trap: Using HLL for exact distinct users for invoices
gotchas.correction: Wrong tool—HLL is approximate and does not store IDs; use an exact store when billing requires precise distincts.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting the geohash boundary problem (or poles/±180°)
gotchas.correction: Always expand to neighbors (or use an H3 k-ring), then apply exact distance filtering.

gotchas.trap: Saying “consistent hashing” when the system uses fixed hash slots (e.g. Redis Cluster 16384)
gotchas.correction: The principle is minimal remapping; implementations may use fixed slots—note the DDIA partitioning naming caveat.
